program_overview.title: Complete App Development Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The whole app landscape in one honest arc: Flutter as your production stack, real backends, then working literacy in native iOS and Android.
program_overview.description:
App development hiring wants a specific shape of developer: deep in one cross-platform stack that ships products fast, and literate enough in native iOS and Android to go deeper when a product demands it. This live online masterclass builds exactly that shape: Flutter and Dart as the production road, UI, state management, navigation done properly, then the product layer, storage, REST APIs, Firebase, app backends with Node, testing, plus honest survey weeks of React Native and PWAs so the alternatives are understood rather than feared. Then the native literacy phase: a real month in Swift with SwiftUI, a real month in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose. A finale month ships a capstone app and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: One production stack, not a four-framework blur: Flutter carries the building; native months add literacy
The product layer included: storage, APIs, Firebase and app backends, where real apps live
Native literacy on both platforms: Swift with SwiftUI, Kotlin with Compose, taught for judgment
Alternatives surveyed honestly: React Native and PWAs explained, so stack choices are informed
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this app development course cover?
faqs.answer: Flutter and Dart as the production stack: UI, state management and navigation properly, then the product layer, local storage, REST APIs, Firebase, app backends with Node, testing, plus honest survey weeks of React Native and PWAs. Then native literacy: a month of Swift with SwiftUI and a month of Kotlin with Jetpack Compose. A finale month ships a capstone app and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn app development properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Why Flutter first, and then native months?
faqs.answer: Because that is the shape hiring actually wants: deep in one cross-platform stack that ships products fast, plus enough native fluency to read platform documentation, use platform channels and know when a feature demands going native. Four frameworks at equal depth in one course would be a tour, not a skill; one deep stack plus two literacy months is a profile.

faqs.question: Do I need a Mac?
faqs.answer: Not to take the course. Flutter, Android and the backend work run on any computer, and that is where your hands-on depth lives. The Swift month is the one place Apple's rules bite: full iOS building needs a Mac, so learners without one follow the instructor's live Xcode session and practice Swift itself in browser playgrounds, while learners with a Mac run everything locally. We say this upfront rather than let it surprise you in month seven.
